title: Insert into a Binary Search Tree
summary: Add the absent value val to a binary search tree and return a root of a valid BST containing exactly the original values and the added value.

contractDetails.constraints: 0–10000 nodes with distinct values in [−100000000,100000000]. val is in the same range and absent from the tree. Input and result use level-order values with null for missing children.
contractDetails.output-checking: Serialize the returned root with null child positions. Verify strict BST ordering and the complete original value set plus val. Accept alternative valid shapes. No original-node identity constraint is imposed.

statement: Add the absent value val to a binary search tree and return a root of a valid BST containing exactly the original values and the added value. Any valid resulting shape is acceptable. Values in a node’s left subtree must be smaller and values in its right subtree must be larger.

examples.explanation: One valid shape inserts 5 as the left child of 6.
The new value becomes the root.
Zero belongs in the right subtree of −2 and the left subtree of 1.

constraints: 0–10000 nodes with distinct values in [−100000000,100000000]. val is in the same range and absent from the tree. Input and result use level-order values with null for missing children.
hints: Conceptual: BST comparisons identify a direction for the new value.
Directional: Follow the same path that would search for val.
Implementation: At the first missing child on that path, attach a new node. If the root is absent, create the root.
complexityAnalysis: O(h) time and O(1) auxiliary solution space for iterative insertion, excluding the new node.
